content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a vanilla scent using extract, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sterilize the glass maceration jars (20 minutes)
Step 2. Label the finished scent bottles (5 minutes)
Step 3. Slice the vanilla beans lengthwise (15 minutes)
Step 4. Measure out the high-proof alcohol base (5 minutes)
Step 5. Combine the aged extract with the carrier oil (10 minutes)
Step 6. Research different vanilla bean varieties (2 hours)
Step 7. Filter the final mixture through a fine mesh (30 minutes)
Step 8. Order glass dropper bottles online (10 minutes)
Step 9. Purchase premium grade vanilla beans (1 hour)
Step 10. Wash the workspace surfaces (15 minutes)
Step 11. Receive the delivery of dropper bottles (3 days)
Step 12. Inventory existing scent supplies (30 minutes)
Step 13. Print custom ingredient labels (15 minutes)
Step 14. Calibrate the digital kitchen scale (10 minutes)
Step 15. Prepare a dark storage area for aging (20 minutes)
Step 16. Sanitize the measuring beakers (15 minutes)
Step 17. Organize the botanical library (1 hour)
Step 18. Set a budget for the project (10 minutes)
Step 19. Submerge the sliced beans in alcohol (5 minutes)
Step 20. Select the appropriate carrier oil (30 minutes)
Step 21. Clear a dedicated workbench (1 hour)
Step 22. Compare prices of bulk suppliers (1 hour)
Step 23. Sharpen the paring knife (10 minutes)
Step 24. Rinse the graduated cylinders (10 minutes)
Step 25. Design the logo for the scent (4 hours)
Step 26. Sweep the laboratory floor (20 minutes)
Step 27. Read reviews of vanilla bean vendors (45 minutes)
Step 28. Let the vanilla beans macerate in the dark (2 months)
Step 29. Source organic fixatives (2 days)
Step 30. Clean the cutting board (5 minutes)
Step 31. Decant the extract into a clean bowl (10 minutes)
Step 32. Write down the scent recipe (15 minutes)
Step 33. Assemble the packaging boxes (1 hour)
Step 34. Check the mail for supplier catalogs (5 minutes)
Step 35. Prepare the shipping station (40 minutes)
Step 36. Look up aromatherapy safety guidelines (1 hour)
Step 37. Purchase the chosen carrier oil (1 day)
Step 38. Plug in the task lighting (2 minutes)
Step 39. Apply labels to the packaging (30 minutes)
Step 40. Wash the amber glass storage bottles (15 minutes)
